timeline.label: Filed FY2025 Form 20-F: revenue $38.4B, net income to parent $2.4B (down from $6.2B), impairments and weaker iron ore prices
Paid $5.9B in dividends FY2025 ($3.6B to parent equity holders) while repaying net borrowings
Vale Base Metals segment reports copper/nickel growth focus; iron solutions remains majority of revenue
Ongoing Brumadinho and dam de-characterization cash payments ($1.25B in FY2025 operating cash)
Mosaic activist SC-13D/A filing on VALE (inventory; holder/strategic interest context)
Brumadinho dam collapse legacy: remediation and compensation obligations continue to affect operating cash
Post-Samarco/Brazil crisis governance reforms; safety and tailings governance elevated in capital allocation

industry.structure: Global iron ore is an oligopoly (Vale, Rio Tinto, BHP) with high barriers (ore body quality, logistics, capital). Vale is the largest seaborne iron ore supplier from Brazil's Carajás and southeastern systems.
industry.share_shift: Chinese steel demand and domestic mine output drive seaborne trade flows; Vale gains when Brazilian grades are preferred but loses when China favors domestic or Australian blend.
industry.trend: Energy-transition metals (copper, nickel via Vale Base Metals) are growing strategic focus, but iron ore still dominates revenue and cash. ESG, tailings safety, and dam decommissioning remain structural cost and risk items.
